dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Could it be resold to the Knights of Favonius?

dialogues.speaker: Bernhard
dialogues.text: This is indeed a method, and sometimes, the Knights will spontaneously count their personal needs.

dialogues.speaker: Bernhard
dialogues.text: If residents have used goods that they are willing to sell, and the knights do not mind, they can make a deal directly to reduce the waste of materials.

dialogues.speaker: Bernhard
dialogues.text: In the same way, the inhabitants could speak directly to the knights if they need something.

dialogues.speaker: Bernhard
dialogues.text: Maybe someone recently wanted to buy something, but didn't realize that these owners had a lot of stuff they couldn't sell.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright! Well, it's up to you to bridge the gap, Bernhard.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Bernhard leaves for the Order to look at the purchase needs...

dialogues.speaker: Bernhard
dialogues.text: It just so happens that a lot of people want to buy used goods these days, and they can resell most of the surplus goods to them.

dialogues.speaker: Bernhard
dialogues.text: Some of the knights also chipped in to pay for our hard work.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay! The thrift crisis is solved, and everyone's needs are met!
